# The event log

<!-- Generated by `bun scripts/event-log-doc.ts --write` from packages/core/src/event/durable.ts. Do not edit by hand: test/release/event-log-doc.test.ts fails when this file differs from what the generator prints. -->

Every session is an append-only log of events. Everything else (the conversation, what the agent is doing, the
request sent to the model) is computed from it. This page is the log's specification: the rules every log follows,
how to read one, and every event with its fields. The fields and descriptions below are generated from the schema
the program itself decodes with, so they are what this build writes and reads.

## Where a log is

Each session is one SQLite database, `~/.local/share/light-harness/sessions/<session id>.db` (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/light-harness/sessions/`
when that is set), in WAL mode, so `-wal` and `-shm` files sit beside it, with `-lock` and `-holder` files that
say which process works in it. The log is the table `event`:

| Column | What |
| --- | --- |
| `session_id` | the session's ID |
| `seq` | the event's position in the session's log |
| `type` | the event type, such as `tool.called` |
| `v` | the version of that type's data |
| `time` | milliseconds since the Unix epoch, from the writer's clock: for display, never for ordering |
| `data` | the event's data as canonical JSON (sorted keys, no spaces), so equal data is equal bytes |

The other tables (`session`, `message`, `inbox`) are projections: they are rewritten from the events in the
same transaction as each append, and rebuilding them from the log gives the same rows. `request` is the ledger of
model calls, kept beside the log. The database's `PRAGMA user_version` is the schema version, 4 in this build;
a build refuses a file of another version rather than misread it.

## The rules

- **Append-only.** Events are only ever added. The database has triggers that refuse an `UPDATE` or a `DELETE` on
  `event` (`the event log is append-only`). Nothing is deleted: an undo, a compaction and a refused response
  are later events that name a range of `seq`; the earlier events stay.
- **Dense `seq`.** A session's events are numbered 1, 2, 3, ... with no gaps, and `seq` is the only order. A
  fork's own events start after its fork point (below).
- **One writer.** One process at a time holds a session (its `-lock` file); every append goes through the program's
  reducer, which rejects an event that is illegal in the state the log is in (a tool result for a call that was
  never made, a second terminal event for a step).
- **Strict decoding.** Each event type has one validator. An object has exactly the fields listed below: an unknown
  field is an error, and a field is absent only where the table says it may be (fields added to a shape after it
  was first written); otherwise an absent value is an explicit `null`. An event of an unknown type, or of a version
  the build does not read, is an error too: a reader must stop there rather than skip it, because a log folded with
  a hole in it gives a wrong state.
- **Versions.** Every event type has a version, `v`. Nothing has been released, so every type is at version 1 and
  shapes were still changed in place. From the first release on, a change to an event's data is a new version, and
  the program keeps a decoder for the old one. A new event type, or a new value of an enumeration, needs no new
  version.
- **Frozen text.** Text the model saw (a tool's output, an appended instruction, a checkpoint) is stored in the event
  as it was sent and is never rendered again, so a request can be rebuilt from the log byte for byte.

## Sessions that come from other sessions

- **A fork** (`lineage.kind: "fork"` in its `session.created`) shares its parent's history up to the fork point,
  `throughSeq`. Its own file holds only its own events, from `throughSeq + 1` on (its `session.created` is at that
  `seq`); its first `throughSeq` events are the parent's, read from the parent's file (the `session` table has
  `parent_id` and `parent_seq`). The parent may still be working: only events up to the fork point are read, and
  those never change. A fork whose parent's file is gone still opens and runs, but its inherited events can no
  longer be read.
- **A subagent** (`lineage.kind: "spawn"`) is a session of its own with a fresh log from `seq` 1. The parent's
  log records only that it started and ended (`spawn.started`, `spawn.ended`) and the tool call that started it;
  the child's events are in the child's file.
- **A replay** (`lineage.kind: "replay"`) has a log of its own from `seq` 1 that names the recorded session it
  replays (`sourceSessionId`) and how far (`throughSeq`).

## Reading a log safely

Open the database read-only and never write to it. A read-only connection takes no lock, so it works while the
session is open in another process; WAL mode lets it read beside the writer, and it sees only committed events. Do
not copy a live database file without its `-wal` file: the newest events may be there. With Bun:

```ts
import { Database } from "bun:sqlite"

const db = new Database(`${process.env.HOME}/.local/share/light-harness/sessions/ses_1f0c3a9e.db`, { readonly: true })
for (const row of db.query("SELECT seq, type, v, time, data FROM event ORDER BY seq").all() as { seq: number; type: string; v: number; time: number; data: string }[]) {
  const data = JSON.parse(row.data)
  console.log(row.seq, row.type, data)
}
db.close()
```

To check events against the schema as the program does, decode each row with `decodeEvent` from
`packages/core/src/event/decode.ts`; it throws on an unknown type, an unknown version or invalid data. Two other ways
to see events: `lh --json "<prompt>"` prints every event of a run as one JSON line as it is written (each
with its `seq`), and `bun scripts/export-trace.ts <session id> -o <file>` exports a session's requests.

## An example: one turn

The events of a session in which the user asked `what does notes.txt say?` and the model read the file and answered.
They come from a run of the program with a scripted model, shortened: IDs, paths, the system prompt and the tool
list are cut down. Each line is one row: `seq`, `type`, `v` and the `data` column (`time` is left out).

```json
{"seq":1,"type":"session.created","v":1,"data":{"cwd":"/home/me/proj","lineage":null,"settings":{"model":"gpt-6-luna","reasoningEffort":"low"},"title":null}}
{"seq":2,"type":"inbox.enqueued","v":1,"data":{"content":[{"text":"what does notes.txt say?","type":"text"}],"delivery":"steer","messageId":"msg_u1","origin":null}}
{"seq":3,"type":"execution.started","v":1,"data":{"executionId":"exe_1"}}
{"seq":4,"type":"snapshot.taken","v":1,"data":{"id":"b550fc71d49e","messageId":null,"point":"delivery"}}
{"seq":5,"type":"baseline.set","v":1,"data":{"instructions":"You are a coding agent. You work in a terminal on the user's machine and act only through the tools you are given: …","sources":[{"fingerprint":"9c1e…","source":"environment"}],"tools":[{"description":"Read a file …","inputSchema":{"type":"object"},"name":"read"}]}}
{"seq":6,"type":"inbox.delivered","v":1,"data":{"messageId":"msg_u1"}}
{"seq":7,"type":"step.started","v":1,"data":{"attempt":1,"messageId":"msg_a1","model":"gpt-6-luna"}}
{"seq":8,"type":"tool.called","v":1,"data":{"callId":"c1","input":"{\"path\":\"notes.txt\"}","messageId":"msg_a1","name":"read","providerData":null}}
{"seq":9,"type":"tool.started","v":1,"data":{"callId":"c1","effect":"read","messageId":"msg_a1","run":{"mode":"auto","origin":"builtin","paths":[{"given":"notes.txt","place":"workspace","real":"/home/me/proj/notes.txt","relative":"notes.txt"}],"sandbox":null}}}
{"seq":10,"type":"tool.settled","v":1,"data":{"attachments":[],"callId":"c1","display":{"lines":1,"offset":1,"path":"notes.txt","totalLines":1},"messageId":"msg_a1","outcome":"success","output":"1\thello","truncation":null}}
{"seq":11,"type":"step.ended","v":1,"data":{"finish":"tool_calls","messageId":"msg_a1","usage":{"cachedInputTokens":0,"inputTokens":5000,"outputTokens":20,"reasoningTokens":0}}}
{"seq":12,"type":"step.started","v":1,"data":{"attempt":1,"messageId":"msg_a2","model":"gpt-6-luna"}}
{"seq":13,"type":"text.ended","v":1,"data":{"messageId":"msg_a2","providerData":null,"text":"notes.txt says hello."}}
{"seq":14,"type":"step.ended","v":1,"data":{"finish":"stop","messageId":"msg_a2","usage":{"cachedInputTokens":4992,"inputTokens":5100,"outputTokens":8,"reasoningTokens":0}}}
{"seq":15,"type":"execution.succeeded","v":1,"data":{"executionId":"exe_1","verification":{"status":"not_configured"}}}
```

Read in order:

- 1: the session exists, in `/home/me/proj`, with its model settings.
- 2 to 6: the user's message is admitted to the inbox (`steer`: deliver at the next step boundary), the process
  claims the session (`execution.started`), records the workspace before the input (`snapshot.taken` at
  `delivery`, what an undo of this turn goes back to), freezes the system prompt and tool list (`baseline.set`,
  only before the first step and after a compaction), and delivers the message.
- 7 to 11: one model call (a step). The model asks for a tool call, written before anything runs
  (`tool.called`); the approval layer lets it run and records under what (`tool.started`); its one result is
  stored as the model will see it (`tool.settled`); the step ends with the provider's usage.
- 12 to 14: a second step; the model answers with text and stops.
- 15: nothing is left to do; the claim is released, and `verification` says what "done" rests on (here: no
  checks are configured).

A file edit would add `snapshot.taken` at `step_start` and `step_end` around the step's tools; a question would
add `approval.requested` and `approval.answered` between `tool.called` and `tool.started`.

## The events

55 event types, in 14 groups. In the tables, "Required: may be absent" marks a field that can be left out of `data`; every other field is always present (inside an object that is itself present), and a type that ends in "or `null`" may be `null`. A field inside an object or a list is written with dots (`work.command`, `paths[].real`); "when `kind: ...`" marks the fields of one shape of a union. Shapes used in several places are under [Shared shapes](#shared-shapes).

| Group | Events |
| --- | --- |
| session lifecycle | [`session.created`](#sessioncreated), [`settings.changed`](#settingschanged), [`session.renamed`](#sessionrenamed), [`session.archived`](#sessionarchived), [`session.unarchived`](#sessionunarchived) |
| frozen request prefix | [`baseline.set`](#baselineset), [`instruction.appended`](#instructionappended), [`agent.switched`](#agentswitched) |
| inbox | [`inbox.enqueued`](#inboxenqueued), [`inbox.delivery_changed`](#inboxdelivery_changed), [`inbox.cancelled`](#inboxcancelled), [`inbox.delivered`](#inboxdelivered), [`turn.ended`](#turnended), [`synthetic.appended`](#syntheticappended) |
| execution | [`execution.started`](#executionstarted), [`execution.resumed`](#executionresumed), [`execution.succeeded`](#executionsucceeded), [`execution.failed`](#executionfailed), [`execution.interrupt_requested`](#executioninterrupt_requested), [`execution.interrupted`](#executioninterrupted) |
| step: one model call | [`step.started`](#stepstarted), [`step.ended`](#stepended), [`step.failed`](#stepfailed), [`step.refused`](#steprefused), [`retry.scheduled`](#retryscheduled) |
| model output | [`text.ended`](#textended), [`reasoning.ended`](#reasoningended) |
| tools | [`tool.called`](#toolcalled), [`tool.started`](#toolstarted) |
| approval | [`approval.requested`](#approvalrequested), [`approval.answered`](#approvalanswered), [`approval.denied`](#approvaldenied), [`taint.noticed`](#taintnoticed), [`taint.cleared`](#taintcleared), [`tool.settled`](#toolsettled) |
| spawned work: subagents and background commands | [`spawn.started`](#spawnstarted), [`spawn.ended`](#spawnended) |
| replay | [`replay.call`](#replaycall), [`replay.diverged`](#replaydiverged), [`replay.ended`](#replayended) |
| compaction | [`compaction.started`](#compactionstarted), [`compaction.repair_requested`](#compactionrepair_requested), [`compaction.ended`](#compactionended), [`compaction.failed`](#compactionfailed) |
| workspace snapshots | [`snapshot.taken`](#snapshottaken), [`snapshot.unavailable`](#snapshotunavailable), [`snapshot.coverage`](#snapshotcoverage) |
| verification | [`checks.started`](#checksstarted), [`checks.finished`](#checksfinished), [`checks.failed`](#checksfailed) |
| history ranges and the workspace that goes with them | [`revert.started`](#revertstarted), [`history.reverted`](#historyreverted), [`revert.undo_started`](#revertundo_started), [`history.restored`](#historyrestored), [`revert.failed`](#revertfailed) |

## Session lifecycle

### `session.created`

Version 1.

A session exists. Always the first event of a session's own log. For a fork, `lineage` names the parent and the last inherited `seq`, and this event's `seq` is `throughSeq + 1`; a subagent and a replay start at 1. `settings` is the model and reasoning effort the session starts with; a fork states its own, which may be the parent's.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cwd` | string, not empty | yes |
| `title` | string, or `null` | yes |
| `lineage` | [lineage](#lineage), or `null` | yes |
| `settings` | [sessionSettings](#sessionsettings) | yes |

### `settings.changed`

Version 1.

The session's model or reasoning effort changed, from here on. Accepted only at a step boundary, with or without a running execution, and only if something actually changes. The next request's `params` block differs from the previous request's: a legitimate break of the cached prefix, which `checkPrefix` is told about through this event.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | string, not empty | yes |
| `reasoningEffort` | string, not empty, or `null` | yes |

### `session.renamed`

Version 1.

The session's title was set.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | yes |

### `session.archived`

Version 1.

The session was hidden from the default list. Nothing is deleted from its log; the workspace snapshots no revert or undo of it could still restore are dropped. Rejected for a session that is already archived.

No fields: `data` is `{}`.

### `session.unarchived`

Version 1.

The session was restored to the default list. Rejected for a session that is not archived.

No fields: `data` is `{}`.

## Frozen request prefix

### `baseline.set`

Version 1.

The system prompt and tool list every request uses from here on, with their text frozen (context rule 2). Recorded before the session's first step and again only after a compaction, which is the one place the prefix may change. `sources` lists the instruction sources folded into `instructions`, each with the fingerprint of the value it had; a source appears at most once.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `instructions` | string | yes |
| `tools` | list of [toolSpec](#toolspec) | yes |
| `sources` | list of [instructionFingerprint](#instructionfingerprint) | yes |

### `instruction.appended`

Version 1.

An instruction that changed after the baseline (the date, an edited AGENTS.md, a skill list) became part of history as a new message, with its text frozen here (context rule 3). `source` names what it describes so a later compaction can fold the newest text per source into the next baseline. `fingerprint` identifies the value `text` gives the model for that source; `null` means the message tells the model the source is gone. `detail` is set for the sources that are never part of the baseline (the MCP catalogue, the skill index, memory): what the text carries, as fields.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `source` | string, not empty | yes |
| `text` | string | yes |
| `fingerprint` | string, not empty, or `null` | yes |
| `detail` | [instructionDetail](#instructiondetail) | may be absent |

### `agent.switched`

Version 1.

The agent the session runs as changed: a role kept as a file, with instructions, restrictions and sometimes a model (`agents/`). `to` is the definition as it was when it was selected (its instructions, the restrictions in force, its fingerprint), so the session never reads the file again; `null` switches the agent off. `from` names the agent before.

Written in two places. With `messageId: null`, before the session's first baseline: the session starts as the agent, whose instructions are then a section of that baseline (a subagent started as an agent, or under a parent that runs as one, has it from its creation). Otherwise at a step boundary, right after the `instruction.appended` message (source `agent`) that gives the model the new instructions, and `messageId` is that message: the baseline is frozen, so a switch is an appended message. From this event on every call is checked against `to.restrictions` before the approval layer decides it.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty, or `null` | yes |
| `from` | string, not empty, or `null` | yes |
| `to` | [agentRecord](#agentrecord), or `null` | yes |

## Inbox

### `inbox.enqueued`

Version 1.

Input was admitted and is waiting to be delivered. `messageId` is the ID the message will have once delivered. `origin` is `null` when the user wrote it; otherwise it names the harness component that produced it (a finished background command, a wake-up) and the item is synthetic. `untrusted` is set when the content came from outside the harness (a webhook's body, a networked check's output): a taint source, recorded with the admission.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `origin` | string, not empty, or `null` | yes |
| `delivery` | one of `"steer"`, `"queue"` | yes |
| `content` | [content](#content) | yes |
| `untrusted` | [untrustedInput](#untrustedinput) | may be absent |

### `inbox.delivery_changed`

Version 1.

A waiting item was switched between steer and queue.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `delivery` | one of `"steer"`, `"queue"` | yes |

### `inbox.cancelled`

Version 1.

A waiting item was withdrawn before delivery. It never becomes a message.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |

### `inbox.delivered`

Version 1.

A waiting item became a message in history, at a step boundary (cancel rule 8). The item leaves the inbox in the same transaction. A queued item that follows a turn is delivered right after that turn's `turn.ended`.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |

### `turn.ended`

Version 1.

The turn in progress has its answer and the verification gate let it end, but a queued message waits, so the execution carries on with that message instead of ending: the next event is its `inbox.delivered`. `verification` is what `execution.succeeded` would have said, so a turn says what "done" rests on whether or not something was queued behind it. A queued message waits for this; a steer never does.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verification` | [verificationOutcome](#verificationoutcome) | yes |

### `synthetic.appended`

Version 1.

The harness itself added a message to history at a step boundary, without going through the inbox: the marker that the previous response was interrupted (cancel rule 6), the single empty-response nudge, a check result. `origin` names the kind; see `HARNESS_ORIGIN` for the ones the step loop writes.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `origin` | string, not empty | yes |
| `content` | [content](#content) | yes |

## Execution

### `execution.started`

Version 1.

The write-ahead claim: this process started working on the session. A session with a claim and no terminal event after a restart was cut off by a crash and is recovered.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `executionId` | string, not empty | yes |

### `execution.resumed`

Version 1.

A new process took up a claimed execution again. When the claim was still `running`, the previous process crashed, and the resume counts toward the crash-resume cap (`crashResumes`); when it was `suspended` by a clean shutdown, it does not.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `executionId` | string, not empty | yes |

### `execution.succeeded`

Version 1.

The session ran until it had nothing left to do: the inbox is empty and the model has answered everything it was given. Releases the claim. `verification` is what the gate found at that point, so "done" always says what it rests on: passing checks, no checks, or failing checks that were left unresolved and why.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `executionId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `verification` | [verificationOutcome](#verificationoutcome) | yes |

### `execution.failed`

Version 1.

The execution gave up (a non-retryable error, attempts exhausted). Releases the claim. `cause` is `approval` when it was ended because a call needed the user's approval and nobody was there to give it (the unattended behaviour `stop`), and `replay` when a replay session's replay ended where the model had not answered (it left the recording, or the recording itself ends there): not a failure of anything, but the execution has no answer to end on. Absent for every other failure.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `executionId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `message` | string | yes |
| `cause` | one of `"approval"`, `"replay"` | may be absent |

### `execution.interrupt_requested`

Version 1.

An interrupt was asked for: the user cancelled, or the process is shutting down. Written the moment the abort fires, before any tool has stopped, so a crash in the middle of stopping cannot turn a cancel back into work. From here until `execution.interrupted` with the same `reason`, only events that wind the execution down are accepted: flushing visible text, settling calls, closing the open step or compaction as interrupted, and the interrupt marker. Recovery that finds a requested interrupt finishes it the same way and never resumes the work.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `executionId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `reason` | one of `"user"`, `"shutdown"` | yes |

### `execution.interrupted`

Version 1.

The execution was interrupted, as asked for by the `execution.interrupt_requested` before it. `reason` is explicit and has no default: `user` releases the claim, `shutdown` keeps it for the next start.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `executionId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `reason` | one of `"user"`, `"shutdown"` | yes |

## Step: one model call

### `step.started`

Version 1.

A model call began under assistant message `messageId`. `attempt` counts within the step's single retry budget: a retry before any durable output keeps the same message, while a retry after output starts a new message with the next `attempt` (retry rule 2). `model` is the model that is called, which is always the session's current `settings.model`; it is repeated here so that a reader of the event stream needs no projection.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `attempt` | integer ≥ 1 | yes |
| `model` | string, not empty | yes |

### `step.ended`

Version 1.

The model call completed. Every tool call of the step was settled before this.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `finish` | one of `"stop"`, `"tool_calls"`, `"length"` | yes |
| `usage` | [usage](#usage), or `null` | yes |

### `step.failed`

Version 1.

The step ended without completing: provider failure, interruption, crash or harness error. The single terminal event of the step; every tool call was settled before it. Output recorded so far stays in history.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `error` | [stepError](#steperror) | yes |
| `usage` | [usage](#usage), or `null` | yes |

### `step.refused`

Version 1.

The provider refused. The step stays in the log, but every message from `excludeFromSeq` up to this event is excluded from model history, so the refused content cannot trip the filter again (retry rule 7). A compaction in that range is excluded with it: its checkpoint may quote what was refused, and history goes back to what it was before it. `message` is the refusal text for display.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `message` | string | yes |
| `excludeFromSeq` | integer ≥ 1 | yes |
| `usage` | [usage](#usage), or `null` | yes |

### `retry.scheduled`

Version 1.

A retry of the model call was scheduled after `error`. `attempt` is the number of the attempt that will run after `delayMs`.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `attempt` | integer ≥ 2 | yes |
| `delayMs` | integer ≥ 0 | yes |
| `error` | [providerError](#providererror) | yes |

## Model output

### `text.ended`

Version 1.

The model finished a piece of text; `text` is the whole piece. Also written for the visible partial text of an interrupted step (cancel rule 3).

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `text` | string | yes |
| `providerData` | any JSON (`null` included) | yes |

### `reasoning.ended`

Version 1.

The model finished a reasoning item. `text` is the readable summary; `providerData` is the provider's opaque payload, replayed verbatim. Partial reasoning is never recorded.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `text` | string | yes |
| `providerData` | any JSON (`null` included) | yes |

## Tools

### `tool.called`

Version 1.

The model asked for a tool call. Written before anything runs; if this write fails, nothing runs (cancel rule 1). `input` is the argument text exactly as the model produced it. Keyed by `(messageId, callId)` because providers reuse call IDs across steps.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `callId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `name` | string, not empty | yes |
| `input` | string | yes |
| `providerData` | any JSON (`null` included) | yes |

### `tool.started`

Version 1.

The tool began executing. From here a side effect may have happened, so a call that is started but never settled is settled as `effect_unknown` (or `error`), never as `not_started`. `effect` is the tool's effect class at the moment it started: a `read` call has no side effect and can never settle as `effect_unknown`, and crash recovery settles an orphan from this field, never from the tool registry of the build that restarts.

`run` is what the approval layer let the call run under: the mode, where the tool comes from, the path facts the decision was made from, and for a command whether it runs in the sandbox (`sandbox: null`: it does not) and with which extra access. Taint is derived from these facts, never from the disk again. Absent when the approval layer is off.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `callId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `effect` | one of `"read"`, `"write"`, `"exec"`, `"network"` | yes |
| `run` | [callRun](#callrun) | may be absent |

## Approval

### `approval.requested`

Version 1.

The user is asked whether a call may run. Recorded with everything the decision was made from and everything the question shows: the mode, the path facts and the escalation the model asked for, the question with its choices and what each remembers, what the question is about (`needs`), and how the call runs if the answer approves (`then`). The call stays `pending`. One question per call.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `callId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `mode` | one of `"ask"`, `"auto"`, `"full"` | yes |
| `paths` | list of [storedPathFact](#storedpathfact) | yes |
| `escalation` | [storedEscalation](#storedescalation), or `null` | yes |
| `question` | [storedQuestion](#storedquestion) | yes |
| `needs` | list of [storedNeed](#storedneed) | yes |
| `then` | [storedRunDecision](#storedrundecision) | yes |

### `approval.answered`

Version 1.

The user's answer to the question of this call: the choice, a note if they wrote one, and the approvals the choice created (`grants`, stamped with this event's own `seq`). Session grants apply from here on; project grants are also kept in the user's data directory, where later sessions of the project read them. An approving answer is followed by `tool.started`, a declining one by `tool.settled` with the refusal.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `callId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `choice` | one of `"once"`, `"session"`, `"project"`, `"deny"` | yes |
| `approve` | boolean | yes |
| `note` | string, or `null` | yes |
| `grants` | list of [grant](#grant) | yes |

### `approval.denied`

Version 1.

The call was refused without anyone being asked: by the policy (`policy`), or because it needed approval and nobody was present (`unattended`; `needs` is what it needed). `agent` is set when the policy that refused it is the restrictions of the agent the session runs as, and names that agent: they are checked before the approval layer, so `paths` is empty (nothing about the call was looked at) and `mode` is the mode in force then. `stop`: the run ends with it. The call's `tool.settled` follows in the same append, with the text the model sees.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `callId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `mode` | one of `"ask"`, `"auto"`, `"full"` | yes |
| `paths` | list of [storedPathFact](#storedpathfact) | yes |
| `escalation` | [storedEscalation](#storedescalation), or `null` | yes |
| `reason` | one of `"policy"`, `"unattended"` | yes |
| `needs` | list of [storedNeed](#storedneed) | yes |
| `stop` | boolean | yes |
| `agent` | string, not empty | may be absent |

### `taint.noticed`

Version 1.

The session became tainted: content from a source the harness does not control is in the conversation. `source` is the first such result and `text` the sentence the user is shown, once. From here on anything that can send data out asks again. Derived state is not stored: this records that the user was told, and what.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | [storedTaintSource](#storedtaintsource) | yes |
| `text` | string | yes |

### `taint.cleared`

Version 1.

The user said the conversation is trustworthy again. Taint is derived from the log after this event only.

No fields: `data` is `{}`.

### `tool.settled`

Version 1.

The call's one terminal result. `output` is the text for the model, capped once when produced and replayed byte for byte, including the text that explains a `not_started` or `effect_unknown` outcome.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `callId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `outcome` | one of `"success"`, `"error"`, `"not_started"`, `"effect_unknown"` | yes |
| `output` | string | yes |
| `truncation` | [truncation](#truncation), or `null` | yes |
| `attachments` | list of [blobRef](#blobref) | yes |
| `display` | any JSON (`null` included) | yes |

## Spawned work: subagents and background commands

### `spawn.started`

Version 1.

Work that runs beside the session's own steps began: a subagent (a child session) or a shell command started in the background. Written by the tool call `(messageId, callId)` that started it, before the child session exists and right after the command was spawned. `background`: the call returned at once and the result arrives later as a message; otherwise the call itself waits for it (subagents only). A follow-up message to a child that has ended starts new work with a new `spawnId` for the same child session. `agent` names the agent a new subagent runs as, for display; the child's own log has the record.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spawnId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `callId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `background` | boolean | yes |
| `work` | object, one of the shapes below by `kind` | yes |
| `work.command` | when `kind: "command"`: string | yes |
| `work.logPath` | when `kind: "command"`: string, or `null` | yes |
| `work.sessionId` | when `kind: "subagent"`: string, not empty | yes |
| `work.worktree` | when `kind: "subagent"`: [worktreeRecord](#worktreerecord), or `null` | yes |
| `work.agent` | when `kind: "subagent"`: string, not empty | may be absent |

### `spawn.ended`

Version 1.

Spawned work ended. `outcome`: `completed` (the command exited, with `exitCode`; the child's execution succeeded), `failed` (the child's execution failed, or the work could not be started), `stopped` (on request: the stop tool, or an interrupt of this session, which stops everything it spawned) or `lost` (the harness restarted while it ran). `detail` is one sentence for a person. For a subagent, `usage` is what its model calls cost during this piece of work (rolled up into this session's totals), `tainted` whether its conversation holds untrusted content (this session is tainted from here on, as by a tool result), and `merge` what became of its worktree: merged into this workspace (`files` changed), left on its branch because of `conflicts`, or nothing to merge.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spawnId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `outcome` | one of `"completed"`, `"failed"`, `"stopped"`, `"lost"` | yes |
| `detail` | string | yes |
| `exitCode` | integer, or `null` | yes |
| `usage` | [usage](#usage), or `null` | yes |
| `tainted` | boolean | yes |
| `merge` | object, or `null` | yes |
| `merge.status` | one of `"merged"`, `"conflicts"`, `"nothing"`, `"failed"` | yes |
| `merge.branch` | string, not empty | yes |
| `merge.commit` | string, not empty, or `null` | yes |
| `merge.files` | list of string | yes |
| `merge.conflicts` | list of string | yes |
| `merge.kept` | boolean | yes |

## Replay

### `replay.call`

Version 1.

In a replay session: what became of one call of the replayed model. `matched`: it is a call of the recording (same tool, same arguments) and got the recorded result; `normalised`: the same, equal only after the replay's normalisers; `dropped`: made in a step the recording's user cut short, beyond the calls the recording kept; `diverged`: the call that left the recording (`divergence` is its kind); `off_tape`: made after that. `executed`: the tool ran for real, in the replay's copy of the workspace. `recorded` names the recorded step and call (0-based) of a match. Written right before the call's `tool.settled`.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `callId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `result` | one of `"matched"`, `"normalised"`, `"dropped"`, `"diverged"`, `"off_tape"` | yes |
| `executed` | boolean | yes |
| `recorded` | object, or `null` | yes |
| `recorded.step` | integer ≥ 0 | yes |
| `recorded.call` | integer ≥ 0 | yes |
| `divergence` | string, not empty, or `null` | yes |

### `replay.diverged`

Version 1.

The replay left the recording and carries on in a copy of the workspace: `workspace` is the directory, restored from `snapshot` of the recorded session's working directory (`null`: none was recorded at that point and the copy starts empty). From here the session's tools run for real, in that directory.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace` | string, not empty | yes |
| `snapshot` | string, not empty, or `null` | yes |
| `divergence` | string, not empty | yes |

### `replay.ended`

Version 1.

The replay is over. `outcome`: `identical` (every recorded step was replayed and matched), `diverged` (it left the recording), `unsupported` (the recording does something a replay cannot reproduce) or `incomplete` (it ended for another reason: a provider error, an interrupt, a crash). `reason` is one line; `report` is the divergence report as JSON.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `outcome` | one of `"identical"`, `"diverged"`, `"unsupported"`, `"incomplete"` | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |
| `report` | any JSON (`null` included) | yes |

## Compaction

### `compaction.started`

Version 1.

A compaction began under compaction message `messageId`, and everything its summary request is built from is recorded here, so that request can be rebuilt from the log like any other.
- `trigger`: `auto` (the size estimate of the next request crossed the policy's threshold), `overflow` (the provider rejected a request as too large) or `manual`.
- `mode`: how hard. `normal` aims for the policy's target; `aggressive` (after an overflow, or when a normal one freed too little) keeps a much shorter tail. The policy needs it the next time it decides.
- `keepFromSeq`: the cut. Model-visible messages from this `seq` on are kept word for word; what is visible before it is what the summary request shows the model. Equal to this event's own `seq` when nothing is kept. It may lie inside the turn in progress.
- `prompt`: the one prompt the summary request appends to the step request of the part before the cut, frozen.
- `tokensBefore`: the size (input tokens) the next request was estimated at when this was decided: what the compaction started from.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `trigger` | one of `"auto"`, `"manual"`, `"overflow"` | yes |
| `mode` | one of `"normal"`, `"aggressive"` | yes |
| `keepFromSeq` | integer ≥ 1 | yes |
| `prompt` | string | yes |
| `tokensBefore` | integer ≥ 0 | yes |

### `compaction.repair_requested`

Version 1.

The model's answer to the summary request was not usable, and it is asked once more: from ledger attempt `attempt` on, the summary request is the first one plus `answer` (the rejected answer as it is replayed, cut at the output bound) and `prompt` (what to fix), both frozen here. At most one per compaction.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `attempt` | integer ≥ 2 | yes |
| `answer` | string | yes |
| `prompt` | string | yes |

### `compaction.ended`

Version 1.

The compaction produced its checkpoint. From now on model history is `summary` (the whole checkpoint text, rendered once and frozen here: the summary, the identifier index, the user's messages verbatim) followed by the messages from the `keepFromSeq` of `compaction.started` on. Earlier messages stay in the log, in the UI and within reach of the history tools.
- `source`: where the summary part came from. `model`: the first answer; `repaired`: the answer to the repair request; `fallback`: no usable summary could be had, and the checkpoint was built without the model (index, verbatim user messages and a statement that there is no summary).
- `detail`: for a person, why it is a fallback, or what is still wrong with a summary that was used anyway; `null` when there is nothing to say.
- `tokensAfter`: the size the next request is estimated at with the checkpoint in place. `tokensBefore - tokensAfter` is what was freed.
- `calls`: how many summary requests were sent to the model for this compaction, retries and the repair included. A summary call is a model request that is no step (it writes no `step.started`), so the model requests of a turn are its steps plus the `calls` of its compactions.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `summary` | string | yes |
| `source` | one of `"model"`, `"repaired"`, `"fallback"` | yes |
| `detail` | string, or `null` | yes |
| `tokensAfter` | integer ≥ 0 | yes |
| `usage` | [usage](#usage), or `null` | yes |
| `calls` | integer ≥ 1 | may be absent |

### `compaction.failed`

Version 1.

The compaction did not complete. Model history is unchanged. `calls`: how many summary requests had been sent for it, as on `compaction.ended`.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | string, not empty | yes |
| `error` | [stepError](#steperror) | yes |
| `calls` | integer ≥ 0 | may be absent |

## Workspace snapshots

### `snapshot.taken`

Version 1.

The workspace was recorded as snapshot `id` at this moment. `messageId` names the open step for `step_start` and `step_end` and is `null` otherwise. From these events alone: a step changed what differs between its `step_start` and `step_end` (a step without them could not change files; a step cut short has no `step_end`, and the next snapshot in the log bounds it); a turn changed what differs between the `delivery` snapshot before its input and the last snapshot of the turn; and the snapshot current when a message was delivered is the `delivery` snapshot right before its `inbox.delivered`.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string, not empty | yes |
| `point` | one of `"delivery"`, `"step_start"`, `"step_end"`, `"checks_start"`, `"checks_end"`, `"restore_start"`, `"restore_end"` | yes |
| `messageId` | string, not empty, or `null` | yes |

### `snapshot.unavailable`

Version 1.

No snapshot can be taken from here on, so the session works without undo until a later `snapshot.taken`. Written once per change, not per attempt.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reason` | one of `"git_not_found"`, `"git_too_old"`, `"workspace_invalid"`, `"storage_failed"`, `"snapshot_failed"` | yes |
| `message` | string | yes |

### `snapshot.coverage`

Version 1.

What snapshots leave out, from here on: files too large or unreadable (they cannot be undone) and directories holding their own git repository (nothing inside them is tracked). Written when the set changes, not with every snapshot.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `skipped` | list of [skippedFile](#skippedfile) | yes |
| `nestedRepositories` | list of string | yes |

## Verification

### `checks.started`

Version 1.

The harness began run `run` of the project's checks (1 for the first run of a turn), because the session would otherwise go idle. Its `seq` is the position in the log the checks ran at. Nothing else happens until the run's terminal event, `checks.finished` or `checks.failed`.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `run` | integer ≥ 1 | yes |
| `checks` | list of string, not empty | yes |

### `checks.finished`

Version 1.

Every check of the run has a result. `evidence` is the record of them.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `run` | integer ≥ 1 | yes |
| `evidence` | [verificationEvidence](#verificationevidence) | yes |

### `checks.failed`

Version 1.

The run did not produce results: the execution was interrupted, the process died (recorded by recovery), or the harness failed. It says nothing about the code, and the gate treats it as if the checks had not run.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `run` | integer ≥ 1 | yes |
| `error` | [stepError](#steperror) | yes |

## History ranges and the workspace that goes with them

### `revert.started`

Version 1.

A revert to the state before `fromSeq` began, and its restore is about to run: the write-ahead record of it. `target` is the snapshot the workspace is restored to, `before` the workspace as it is now (the undo point), and `keep` the paths edited by hand since `target` that the user chose to keep. A session that is opened with a revert still open finishes it from these fields. Accepted only while idle.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fromSeq` | integer ≥ 1 | yes |
| `target` | string, not empty | yes |
| `before` | string, not empty | yes |
| `keep` | list of string | yes |

### `history.reverted`

Version 1.

The user rewound the session: every message from `fromSeq` up to this event is excluded from model history. The rows stay. A compaction in that range is excluded like any message, and model history then starts from the latest compaction that is not excluded: reverting to before a compaction undoes it for the model. `restore` is what happened to the workspace: `null` when no file was restored (no snapshot was current at that point), otherwise the record of the restore that `revert.started` announced.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fromSeq` | integer ≥ 1 | yes |
| `restore` | [restoreRecord](#restorerecord), or `null` | yes |

### `revert.undo_started`

Version 1.

The undo of the revert recorded at `revertSeq` began: the workspace is about to be restored to `target`, the snapshot taken before that revert. `before` is the workspace now. The write-ahead record, like `revert.started`.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `revertSeq` | integer ≥ 1 | yes |
| `target` | string, not empty | yes |
| `before` | string, not empty | yes |
| `keep` | list of string | yes |

### `history.restored`

Version 1.

The revert recorded at `revertSeq` was undone: the messages it excluded are part of model history again. `restore` is what happened to the workspace, as in `history.reverted`.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `revertSeq` | integer ≥ 1 | yes |
| `restore` | [restoreRecord](#restorerecord), or `null` | yes |

### `revert.failed`

Version 1.

The open revert, or undo of one, could not restore the workspace. Nothing changed in history.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | string | yes |

Declared in `packages/core/src/event/durable.ts`.

### `lineage`

Where a session came from.
- `fork`: its history is its parent's. It owns no copy of it: its log is the parent's events 1..`throughSeq` followed by its own events, which start at `throughSeq + 1`. `copied` is set when the fork works in a directory of its own: the snapshot of the parent's workspace that was restored into its `cwd` (`null`: the directory was copied as it stood), and the parent's working directory.
- `spawn`: a subagent. It was started by a tool call of `parentSessionId` (the spawned work `spawnId` in the parent's log) with a fresh conversation: it inherits nothing of the parent's history. `depth` is 1 for a child of a session a person started. `worktree` is the git worktree it works in, when it does not share the parent's workspace.
- `replay`: a replay of the recorded session `sourceSessionId` through its event `throughSeq`, against a baseline that differs from the recording's in what `changed` names (the system prompt text, the descriptions of the listed tools, the model settings). `policy` and `strict` are how it was run. Its history is its own; it starts at `seq` 1.

One of these, told apart by `kind`:

`kind: "fork"`

| `parentSessionId` | string, not empty | yes |

| `copied.from` | string, not empty | yes |

`kind: "spawn"`

### `restoreRecord`

What a restore did to the workspace.
- `target`: the snapshot that was restored.
- `before`: the workspace just before the restore. Restoring it undoes the restore.
- `after`: the workspace just after it; equal to `target` unless something was kept. `null` when it could not be taken.
- `changed`: how many files the restore wrote or removed.
- `kept`: paths the restore left as they were, and why: ignored, in a nested repository or never captured (the snapshot module's reasons), or edited by hand since and kept on request. At most `KEPT_LIMIT` are listed; `keptOmitted` counts the rest.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | string, not empty | yes |
| `before` | string, not empty | yes |
| `after` | string, not empty, or `null` | yes |
| `changed` | integer ≥ 0 | yes |
| `kept` | list of objects | yes |
| `kept[].path` | string | yes |
| `kept[].reason` | one of `"ignored"`, `"nested_repository"`, `"not_captured"`, `"hand_edited"` | yes |
| `keptOmitted` | integer ≥ 0 | yes |

Declared in `packages/core/src/event/durable.ts`.

- `reasoningEffort`: provider-interpreted effort such as `"low"` or `"high"`; `null` is the model's default.

### `untrustedInput`

Why an admitted input is content the harness does not control: the firing of a wake-up that carries a webhook's body, or the output of a check that ran with the network or without the sandbox. The session counts as having taken in untrusted content from the admission on (`approval/taint.ts`), so the turn the input starts is decided under that from its first call.

### `usage`

Token counts for one model call, as measured by the provider.
- `inputTokens`: all input tokens, including the cached ones.
- `cachedInputTokens`: the part of `inputTokens` served from the prompt cache.
- `outputTokens`: all output tokens, including reasoning tokens.
- `reasoningTokens`: the part of `outputTokens` spent on reasoning.

So uncached input is `inputTokens - cachedInputTokens`, and the total is `inputTokens + outputTokens`. A provider that reports these differently converts to this shape at its boundary.

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `inputTokens` | integer ≥ 0 | yes |
| `cachedInputTokens` | integer ≥ 0 | yes |
| `outputTokens` | integer ≥ 0 | yes |
| `reasoningTokens` | integer ≥ 0 | yes |

Declared in `packages/core/src/provider/usage.ts`.

### `verificationOutcome`

What the verification gate found when an execution ended as done.
- `not_configured`: verification is off, or no check is configured. Nothing was verified.
- `not_needed`: checks are configured and none ran. Either nothing they cover changed since the last verification that passed, or this turn changed no file: the gate verifies a turn's own work, and a turn that only answered has none. In the second case `unverified` is set when files the checks cover did change since the last verification, outside this turn (the user edited by hand, a turn was undone, an earlier turn ended with its checks failing): they are still to be checked, and are, with everything else, at the end of the next turn that changes a file.
- `passed`: every check that applied passed; `evidence` is that run.
- `unresolved`: checks still fail and the execution ended anyway. `reason` says why it was allowed to: the model reported with the acknowledgement tool that it cannot fix them (`acknowledgement` is what it said), the model had been sent back `maxRounds` times, or the mode is `report`, which never sends the model back.

One of these, told apart by `status`:

`status: "not_configured"`

| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `"not_configured"` | yes |

`status: "not_needed"`

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `"not_needed"` | yes |

`status: "passed"`

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `"passed"` | yes |

| `failing` | list of string, not empty | yes |

| `evidence` | [verificationEvidence](#verificationevidence) | yes |
